metadata.name: lhs_2016_timing_swap
metadata.description:
Latin Hypercube Sampling sweep testing the effect of swapped decision timings
on fork outcome dynamics — 2016-block retarget, full 60-node network.

HYPOTHESIS:
  The two-layer result (hashrate war resolves first, economic adoption second)
  may be a direct artifact of the timing asymmetry between actors:
    Baseline:  pool_decision_interval=600s, econ_switching_cooldown=1800s
    This sweep: pool_decision_interval=1800s, econ_switching_cooldown=600s
  If the ordering is purely timing-driven, swapping should reverse it: economic
  nodes now react 3× faster than pools, potentially causing economic adoption
  to lead hashrate flips rather than follow them.

TIMING PARAMETERS (passed to 3_run_sweep.py at run time):
  --pool-decision-interval 1800     (baseline: 600s)
  --econ-switching-cooldown  600    (baseline: 1800s)
  --user-switching-cooldown  3600   (unchanged — user nodes not part of hypothesis)
  All other timing parameters unchanged from baseline.

DESIGN:
  300 scenarios via Latin Hypercube Sampling (25 per namespace, 12 namespaces)
  2 servers × 6 namespaces each:
    Server 1: ns-0  → ns-5  (sweep_0000–sweep_0149)
    Server 2: ns-6  → ns-11 (sweep_0150–sweep_0299)
  4 active parameters (pool_profitability_threshold and solo_miner_hashrate
  confirmed non-causal — fixed at validated values)
  Full parameter ranges (same as lhs_2016_full_6param) for maximum coverage:
    Ensures timing effects are visible across clean-win, contested, and
    override zones — not just in the PRIM uncertainty box.
  Duration 13000s — consistent with all full-network 2016-block sweeps.
  Seed 2027 — independent samples from existing sweeps.

COMPARISON TARGET:
  Direct comparison with lhs_2016_full_6param (n=692) and
  lhs_2016_full_phase3_merged (n=292) at identical parameter values.
  Key metrics to compare:
    - cascade_time_s (Layer 1 timing)
    - econ_switch_time_s (Layer 2 timing)
    - econ_lag_s = econ_switch_time_s - cascade_time_s (layer gap)
    - Outcome distribution (does v27 win rate change?)
    - Feature importance rank (does pool_committed_split still dominate?)

EXPECTED RUNTIME (per server, 6 namespaces parallel):
  150 scenarios per server, 25 per namespace
  ~4 hours wall-clock per scenario (pod startup + 13000s simulation)
  ~100 hours sequential per namespace → ~100 hours wall-clock (parallel)
